# Engage: Why Do We Have Seasons? {#ss-engage}

::: {.engage-box}
## 🍂 Same Planet, Opposite Seasons

On **January 1**, people in **New York City** bundle up in coats, with an average temperature of about **1 °C (34 °F)**. On the same day, people in **Melbourne, Australia** head to the beach, with an average of about **21 °C (70 °F)**. Six months later, it's the other way around.

Seasons repeat **every year**, and they happen at **opposite times** in the Northern and Southern Hemispheres.

**Our question:** How does Earth's yearly trip around the Sun create seasonal temperature changes?
:::

## Seasons, Weather, and Climate {#ss-weather-climate}

Seasons, weather, and climate are different, but they're connected:

| | What it means | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Weather** | Conditions in the air **right now** (hours to days): temperature, rain, wind, clouds | "It's 3 °C and snowing today." |
| **Season** | Part of the year (months) with a typical pattern of temperature and daylight that **repeats every year** | "NYC winters are cold and dark." |
| **Climate** | The **long-term pattern** of weather in a place, averaged over 30+ years | "NYC has hot summers and cold winters." |

This unit is about **climate change**. We start with seasons because they show how the **Earth–Sun relationship** controls temperature. Once that's clear, you can use the same ideas for changes over much longer times.

# Explore: Modeling the Angle of Insolation {#ss-explore}

::: {.explore-box}
## 🔦 Testing Our Ideas With Models

**Insolation** (*in*coming *sol*ar radi*ation*) is the sunlight energy that reaches a surface. In this Explore you collect data from **two kinds of models**:

- **Part 1, physical models:** a heat lamp (the Sun), an inflatable globe (Earth), thermometers, and grid paper
- **Part 2, computational and visual models:** the Seasons and Ecliptic simulator and data about sunlight around the world

Look for **patterns** in the data. The formal explanation comes later, in the Explain.
:::

## Investigation Launch {#ss-launch}

What changes in **Earth's position with respect to the Sun** might cause seasons? Students usually suggest:

| Possible cause | What changes? | We'll test it in... |
|---|---|---|
| **Distance from the Sun** | Earth's orbit is not a perfect circle, so the distance changes during the year | Part C (distance readout) |
| **Earth's tilt** | Earth's axis is tilted, so the angle of sunlight changes | Parts A, B, C, D |
| **Earth's rotation** | Earth spins once a day | Part C (does spinning change during the year?) |

## Part 1: Using Physical Models {#ss-part1}

In class, groups pointed a **heat lamp** at an **inflatable globe**, taped **3 thermometers** to the globe, and timed the readings with a **stopwatch**. They also shone light onto **large square grid paper**. These virtual versions let you do the same thing on your own.

### Part A: Where Is the Globe Warmest? {#ss-part-a}

The lamp is level with the globe's **equator**. Thermometers are taped at the **equator (0°)**, the **middle latitudes (45° N)**, and **near the pole (75° N)**. Press ▶ or drag the stopwatch to collect data.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
d3 = require("d3@7")
Plot = require("@observablehq/plot@0.6.16")
topo = require("topojson-client@3")
ssRad = Math.PI / 180
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
ssLampTherms = [
  {name: "Equator (0°)", lat: 0, color: "#dc2626"},
  {name: "Middle latitude (45° N)", lat: 45, color: "#d97706"},
  {name: "Near the pole (75° N)", lat: 75, color: "#2563eb"}
]
// Simulated readings from a simple model of the lab: warming rate is proportional
// to how directly the lamp's light hits each spot (cos of latitude).
ssLampTemp = (lat, t) => 21 + 12 * Math.cos(lat * ssRad) * (1 - Math.exp(-t / 5))
viewof ssLampT = Inputs.range([0, 10], {step: 0.5, value: 10, label: "Stopwatch (minutes):"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
ssLampPlay = {
  const b = html`<button style="min-height:44px;padding:8px 18px;border-radius:22px;border:2px solid #0f766e;background:#f0fdfa;color:#115e59;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;">▶ Run the lamp for 10 minutes</button>`;
  b.onclick = () => {
    const input = viewof ssLampT;
    let t = 0;
    input.value = 0; input.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}));
    const timer = setInterval(() => {
      t += 0.5;
      input.value = t;
      input.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}));
      if (t >= 10) clearInterval(timer);
    }, 220);
  };
  return b;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const W = 360, H = 250, cx = 235, cy = 125, R = 92;
  const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("viewBox", `0 0 ${W} ${H}`).attr("role", "img")
    .attr("aria-label", "A heat lamp shining on a globe with three thermometers at the equator, 45 degrees north, and 75 degrees north")
    .style("width", "100%").style("max-width", "480px").style("height", "auto").style("display", "block").style("margin", "auto");
  svg.append("rect").attr("width", W).attr("height", H).attr("rx", 14).attr("fill", "#0b1020");
  // lamp
  svg.append("circle").attr("cx", 34).attr("cy", cy).attr("r", 20).attr("fill", "#fbbf24");
  svg.append("text").attr("x", 34).attr("y", cy + 38).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("fill", "#fde68a").attr("font-size", 11).text("Heat lamp");
  for (let y = cy - 80; y <= cy + 80; y += 20) {
    const dy = y - cy;
    if (Math.abs(dy) >= R) continue;
    const xHit = cx - Math.sqrt(R * R - dy * dy);
    svg.append("line").attr("x1", 58).attr("y1", y).attr("x2", xHit).attr("y2", y).attr("stroke", "#fde047").attr("stroke-opacity", .55).attr("stroke-width", 1.5);
  }
  svg.append("circle").attr("cx", cx).attr("cy", cy).attr("r", R).attr("fill", "#2563eb").attr("stroke", "#93c5fd");
  svg.append("path").attr("d", `M${cx},${cy - R} A${R},${R} 0 0,1 ${cx},${cy + R} Z`).attr("fill", "#0b1020").attr("opacity", .55);
  svg.append("line").attr("x1", cx - R).attr("y1", cy).attr("x2", cx + R).attr("y2", cy).attr("stroke", "#e2e8f0").attr("stroke-dasharray", "3,3").attr("stroke-opacity", .7);
  svg.append("text").attr("x", cx + R - 4).attr("y", cy - 4).attr("text-anchor", "end").attr("fill", "#e2e8f0").attr("font-size", 10).text("equator");
  ssLampTherms.forEach(d => {
    const x = cx - R * Math.cos(d.lat * ssRad), y = cy - R * Math.sin(d.lat * ssRad);
    svg.append("circle").attr("cx", x).attr("cy", y).attr("r", 6).attr("fill", d.color).attr("stroke", "white").attr("stroke-width", 2);
    const T = ssLampTemp(d.lat, ssLampT);
    svg.append("rect").attr("x", x + 10).attr("y", y - 11).attr("width", 54).attr("height", 20).attr("rx", 5).attr("fill", "white");
    svg.append("text").attr("x", x + 37).attr("y", y + 3).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 12).attr("font-weight", 700).attr("fill", d.color).text(`${T.toFixed(1)} °C`);
  });
  svg.append("text").attr("x", W - 10).attr("y", 20).attr("text-anchor", "end").attr("fill", "#e2e8f0").attr("font-size", 12).attr("font-weight", 700).text(`⏱ ${ssLampT.toFixed(1)} min`);
  return svg.node();
}
```

### Part B: How Spread Out Is the Light? {#ss-part-b}

Shine a flashlight (or lamp) straight down onto grid paper, then tilt it. The **same amount of light** comes out of the flashlight every time. Watch how many squares it covers.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof ssBeamAngle = Inputs.range([10, 90], {step: 5, value: 90, label: "Angle of light above the surface (°):"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const a = ssBeamAngle * ssRad;
  const r = 2;                        // beam radius in grid squares
  const along = r / Math.sin(a);      // stretched radius
  const area = Math.PI * r * along;   // squares covered
  const perSquare = 100 / area;       // 100 energy units in the beam
  const W = 360, H = 330;
  const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("viewBox", `0 0 ${W} ${H}`).attr("role", "img")
    .attr("aria-label", `Side view and top view of a light beam hitting a surface at ${ssBeamAngle} degrees`)
    .style("width", "100%").style("max-width", "480px").style("height", "auto").style("display", "block").style("margin", "auto");
  svg.append("rect").attr("width", W).attr("height", H).attr("rx", 14).attr("fill", "#0b1020");
  // side view
  svg.append("text").attr("x", 12).attr("y", 20).attr("fill", "#e2e8f0").attr("font-size", 12).attr("font-weight", 700).text("Side view");
  const gy = 140, gx = 180, s = 14;
  svg.append("rect").attr("x", 10).attr("y", gy).attr("width", W - 20).attr("height", 8).attr("fill", "#a16207");
  const dx = Math.cos(a), dy = Math.sin(a);  // direction toward the light source
  const halfFoot = along * s;
  [-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1].forEach(k => {
    const fx = gx + k * halfFoot;
    svg.append("line").attr("x1", fx - dx * 160).attr("y1", gy - dy * 160).attr("x2", fx).attr("y2", gy)
      .attr("stroke", "#fde047").attr("stroke-width", k === 0 ? 2.5 : 1.5).attr("stroke-opacity", .85);
  });
  svg.append("line").attr("x1", gx - halfFoot).attr("y1", gy + 12).attr("x2", gx + halfFoot).attr("y2", gy + 12).attr("stroke", "#fbbf24").attr("stroke-width", 3);
  svg.append("text").attr("x", gx).attr("y", gy + 26).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("fill", "#fde68a").attr("font-size", 11).text(`lit strip: ${(2 * along).toFixed(1)} squares long`);
  svg.append("text").attr("x", W - 14).attr("y", 20).attr("text-anchor", "end").attr("fill", "#fde68a").attr("font-size", 13).attr("font-weight", 700).text(`${ssBeamAngle}°`);
  // top view grid
  const ty = 180, cols = 22, rows = 10, sq = 14.5, ox = (W - cols * sq) / 2;
  svg.append("text").attr("x", 12).attr("y", ty - 6).attr("fill", "#e2e8f0").attr("font-size", 12).attr("font-weight", 700).text("Top view: grid paper");
  svg.append("rect").attr("x", ox).attr("y", ty).attr("width", cols * sq).attr("height", rows * sq).attr("fill", "#f8fafc");
  const ccx = ox + cols * sq / 2, ccy = ty + rows * sq / 2;
  const glow = Math.min(1, 0.25 + perSquare / 8);
  svg.append("ellipse").attr("cx", ccx).attr("cy", ccy).attr("rx", Math.min(along, cols / 2) * sq).attr("ry", r * sq)
    .attr("fill", d3.interpolateYlOrRd(0.15 + 0.8 * glow)).attr("opacity", .9);
  for (let i = 0; i <= cols; i++) svg.append("line").attr("x1", ox + i * sq).attr("y1", ty).attr("x2", ox + i * sq).attr("y2", ty + rows * sq).attr("stroke", "#94a3b8").attr("stroke-width", .6);
  for (let j = 0; j <= rows; j++) svg.append("line").attr("x1", ox).attr("y1", ty + j * sq).attr("x2", ox + cols * sq).attr("y2", ty + j * sq).attr("stroke", "#94a3b8").attr("stroke-width", .6);
  if (along > cols / 2) svg.append("text").attr("x", ccx).attr("y", ccy + 4).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 11).attr("fill", "#7c2d12").attr("font-weight", 700).text("spreads past the paper!");
  const wrap = d3.create("div");
  wrap.append(() => svg.node());
  wrap.append("div").attr("class", "ss-cards").html(`
    <div class="ss-card"><span class="lab">Area lit</span><b class="big">${area.toFixed(1)} squares</b></div>
    <div class="ss-card"><span class="lab">Energy per square</span><b class="big">${perSquare.toFixed(1)} units</b>(beam = 100 units)</div>
    <div class="ss-card"><span class="lab">Compared with 90°</span><b class="big">${(100 * Math.sin(a)).toFixed(0)}%</b>as much energy per square</div>`);
  return wrap.node();
}
```

### Part C: Carry the Globe Around the Sun {#ss-part-c}

Now tilt the globe **23.5°** and carry it in a circle around the lamp. Keep the axis **pointing the same direction** the whole time (toward the North Star, Polaris), just like the real Earth. Watch the angle of the light hitting **NYC (40.7° N)** and **Melbourne (37.8° S)**.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
ssDecl = (n, eps = 23.44) => -Math.asin(Math.sin(eps * ssRad) * Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * (n + 10) / 365)) / ssRad
ssDayLen = (lat, dec) => {
  const x = -Math.tan(Math.max(-89.9, Math.min(89.9, lat)) * ssRad) * Math.tan(dec * ssRad);
  if (x >= 1) return 0;
  if (x <= -1) return 24;
  return 2 * Math.acos(x) / ssRad / 15;
}
ssNoon = (lat, dec) => Math.max(0, 90 - Math.abs(lat - dec))
ssDistFactor = n => 1 + 0.0334 * Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * (n - 3) / 365)
ssInsol = (lat, n, eps = 23.44, useDist = true) => {
  const dec = ssDecl(n, eps) * ssRad, phi = Math.max(-89.99, Math.min(89.99, lat)) * ssRad;
  const x = Math.max(-1, Math.min(1, -Math.tan(phi) * Math.tan(dec)));
  const w0 = Math.acos(x);
  const q = 1361 / Math.PI * (w0 * Math.sin(phi) * Math.sin(dec) + Math.cos(phi) * Math.cos(dec) * Math.sin(w0));
  return Math.max(0, q * (useDist ? ssDistFactor(n) : 1));
}
ssDistKm = n => 149.6 * (1 - 0.0167 * Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * (n - 3) / 365))
ssDateLabel = n => new Date(2025, 0, n).toLocaleDateString("en-US", {month: "short", day: "numeric"})
ssSeasonNH = n => n >= 79 && n < 172 ? "Spring" : n >= 172 && n < 265 ? "Summer" : n >= 265 && n < 355 ? "Fall" : "Winter"
ssSeasonSH = n => ({Spring: "Fall", Summer: "Winter", Fall: "Spring", Winter: "Summer"})[ssSeasonNH(n)]
ssCities = [
  {name: "NYC", lat: 40.7, color: "#dc2626"},
  {name: "Melbourne", lat: -37.8, color: "#2563eb"}
]
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const n = ssOrbitDay, eps = ssOrbitTilt.startsWith("No") ? 0 : 23.44;
  const dec = ssDecl(n, eps);
  const wrap = d3.create("div").style("display", "flex").style("flex-wrap", "wrap").style("gap", "10px").style("justify-content", "center");
  // --- Top view of the orbit ---
  {
    const W = 340, H = 300, cx = 170, cy = 150, R = 108;
    const svg = wrap.append("svg").attr("viewBox", `0 0 ${W} ${H}`).attr("role", "img")
      .attr("aria-label", `Top view of Earth's orbit on ${ssDateLabel(n)}`)
      .style("width", "100%").style("max-width", "380px").style("height", "auto").style("flex", "1 1 260px");
    svg.append("rect").attr("width", W).attr("height", H).attr("rx", 14).attr("fill", "#0b1020");
    svg.append("text").attr("x", 10).attr("y", 18).attr("fill", "#e2e8f0").attr("font-size", 11).attr("font-weight", 700).text("View from above the North Pole");
    svg.append("circle").attr("cx", cx).attr("cy", cy).attr("r", R).attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke", "#475569").attr("stroke-dasharray", "4,4");
    svg.append("circle").attr("cx", cx).attr("cy", cy).attr("r", 18).attr("fill", "#fbbf24");
    svg.append("text").attr("x", cx).attr("y", cy + 4).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 10).attr("font-weight", 700).attr("fill", "#7c2d12").text("Sun");
    const marks = [[79, "Mar equinox"], [172, "Jun solstice"], [265, "Sep equinox"], [355, "Dec solstice"]];
    marks.forEach(([d, lab]) => {
      const th = (180 + 360 * (d - 172) / 365.25) * ssRad;
      const x = cx + (R + 0) * Math.cos(th), y = cy - R * Math.sin(th);
      svg.append("circle").attr("cx", x).attr("cy", y).attr("r", 3).attr("fill", "#94a3b8");
      const side = Math.abs(Math.cos(th)) > .3;
      const lx = side ? (Math.cos(th) < 0 ? 4 : W - 4) : cx, ly = side ? cy - 22 : cy - (R + 10) * Math.sin(th) + (Math.sin(th) < 0 ? 8 : 0);
      svg.append("text").attr("x", lx).attr("y", ly).attr("text-anchor", side ? (Math.cos(th) < 0 ? "start" : "end") : "middle")
        .attr("font-size", 10).attr("fill", "#cbd5e1").text(lab);
    });
    const th = (180 + 360 * (n - 172) / 365.25) * ssRad;
    const ex = cx + R * Math.cos(th), ey = cy - R * Math.sin(th);
    // day side faces the Sun
    const ang = Math.atan2(cy - ey, cx - ex) / ssRad;
    svg.append("circle").attr("cx", ex).attr("cy", ey).attr("r", 15).attr("fill", "#1e3a8a");
    svg.append("path").attr("d", `M0,-15 A15,15 0 0,1 0,15 Z`).attr("fill", "#60a5fa").attr("transform", `translate(${ex},${ey}) rotate(${ang})`);
    // axis tilt arrow: north pole leans toward +x (fixed direction in space)
    const tl = 26 * Math.sin(eps * ssRad) / Math.sin(23.44 * ssRad);
    if (eps > 0) {
      svg.append("line").attr("x1", ex).attr("y1", ey).attr("x2", ex + tl).attr("y2", ey).attr("stroke", "#f472b6").attr("stroke-width", 3);
      svg.append("text").attr("x", ex + tl + 3).attr("y", ey + 4).attr("font-size", 11).attr("font-weight", 700).attr("fill", "#f9a8d4").text("N");
    }
    svg.append("text").attr("x", 10).attr("y", H - 10).attr("fill", "#94a3b8").attr("font-size", 9.5).text(eps > 0 ? "Pink arrow: the way the North Pole leans (never changes)" : "No tilt: the North Pole points straight up");
  }
  // --- Sun's-eye side view ---
  {
    const W = 340, H = 300, cx = 185, cy = 150, R = 105;
    const svg = wrap.append("svg").attr("viewBox", `0 0 ${W} ${H}`).attr("role", "img")
      .attr("aria-label", `Side view of Earth with sunlight from the left; the Sun is overhead at latitude ${dec.toFixed(1)} degrees`)
      .style("width", "100%").style("max-width", "380px").style("height", "auto").style("flex", "1 1 260px");
    svg.append("rect").attr("width", W).attr("height", H).attr("rx", 14).attr("fill", "#0b1020");
    svg.append("text").attr("x", 10).attr("y", 18).attr("fill", "#e2e8f0").attr("font-size", 11).attr("font-weight", 700).text("Side view: sunlight from the left");
    for (let y = cy - 100; y <= cy + 100; y += 20) {
      const dy = y - cy; if (Math.abs(dy) >= R) continue;
      svg.append("line").attr("x1", 6).attr("y1", y).attr("x2", cx - Math.sqrt(R * R - dy * dy)).attr("y2", y).attr("stroke", "#fde047").attr("stroke-opacity", .45);
    }
    svg.append("circle").attr("cx", cx).attr("cy", cy).attr("r", R).attr("fill", "#60a5fa");
    svg.append("path").attr("d", `M${cx},${cy - R} A${R},${R} 0 0,1 ${cx},${cy + R} Z`).attr("fill", "#0b1020").attr("opacity", .6);
    const d = dec * ssRad;
    const A = [-Math.sin(d), -Math.cos(d)], E = [-Math.cos(d), Math.sin(d)];
    const P = (lat, side = 1) => { const p = lat * ssRad; return [cx + R * (side * Math.cos(p) * E[0] + Math.sin(p) * A[0]), cy + R * (side * Math.cos(p) * E[1] + Math.sin(p) * A[1])]; };
    const lines = [[0, "Equator", "#e2e8f0"], [23.44, "Tropic of Cancer", "#fde68a"], [-23.44, "Tropic of Capricorn", "#fde68a"], [66.56, "Arctic Circle", "#a5f3fc"], [-66.56, "Antarctic Circle", "#a5f3fc"]];
    lines.forEach(([lat, lab, col]) => {
      const p1 = P(lat, 1), p2 = P(lat, -1);
      svg.append("line").attr("x1", p1[0]).attr("y1", p1[1]).attr("x2", p2[0]).attr("y2", p2[1]).attr("stroke", col).attr("stroke-width", 1).attr("stroke-dasharray", lat === 0 ? null : "3,3").attr("stroke-opacity", .85);
      svg.append("text").attr("x", (p1[0] + p2[0]) / 2 + 30).attr("y", (p1[1] + p2[1]) / 2 - 3).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 8.5).attr("fill", col).attr("stroke", "#0b1020").attr("stroke-width", 2.5).attr("paint-order", "stroke").text(lab);
    });
    const np = [cx + 1.22 * R * A[0], cy + 1.22 * R * A[1]], sp = [cx - 1.22 * R * A[0], cy - 1.22 * R * A[1]];
    svg.append("line").attr("x1", sp[0]).attr("y1", sp[1]).attr("x2", np[0]).attr("y2", np[1]).attr("stroke", "#f472b6").attr("stroke-width", 2.5);
    svg.append("text").attr("x", np[0]).attr("y", np[1] - 4).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 11).attr("font-weight", 700).attr("fill", "#f9a8d4").text("N");
    ssCities.forEach(c => {
      const p = P(c.lat, 1);
      svg.append("circle").attr("cx", p[0]).attr("cy", p[1]).attr("r", 5.5).attr("fill", c.color).attr("stroke", "white").attr("stroke-width", 2);
      svg.append("text").attr("x", p[0] - 9).attr("y", p[1] + 4).attr("text-anchor", "end").attr("font-size", 10.5).attr("font-weight", 700).attr("fill", "white").text(c.name);
    });
    const ss = P(dec, 1);
    svg.append("text").attr("x", 8).attr("y", H - 10).attr("font-size", 9.5).attr("fill", "#fde68a").text(`Sun directly overhead at noon: ${Math.abs(dec).toFixed(1)}° ${dec >= 0 ? "N" : "S"}`);
  }
  const nyc = ssNoon(40.7, dec), mel = ssNoon(-37.8, dec);
  const sN = eps > 0 ? ssSeasonNH(n) : "No seasons", sS = eps > 0 ? ssSeasonSH(n) : "No seasons";
  const box = d3.create("div");
  box.append(() => wrap.node());
  box.append("div").attr("class", "ss-cards").html(`
    <div class="ss-card" style="border-color:#dc2626"><span class="lab">NYC · ${sN}</span><b class="big">${nyc.toFixed(0)}°</b>noon Sun angle<br>${ssDayLen(40.7, dec).toFixed(1)} h of daylight</div>
    <div class="ss-card" style="border-color:#2563eb"><span class="lab">Melbourne · ${sS}</span><b class="big">${mel.toFixed(0)}°</b>noon Sun angle<br>${ssDayLen(-37.8, dec).toFixed(1)} h of daylight</div>
    <div class="ss-card"><span class="lab">Earth–Sun distance</span><b class="big">${ssDistKm(n).toFixed(1)}</b>million km (${n >= 365 || n <= 10 ? "near closest" : (n >= 178 && n <= 192 ? "near farthest" : "in between")})</div>`);
  box.append("p").attr("class", "ss-note").text("Orbit drawn as a circle: the real orbit is so close to a circle that its shape is hard to see at this scale. Daylight hours are geometric estimates.");
  return box.node();
}
```

## Making Sense of Part 1 {#ss-making-sense-1}

::: {.student-task}
### ✏️ In your handout: Making Sense of the *What causes seasons? Part 1* Investigation

Complete the **See-Think-Wonder**:

- **See:** What did you observe about temperature (Part A), the spread of light (Part B), and the angle of light during the orbit (Part C)?
- **Think:** What do those observations make you think about how seasons happen?
- **Wonder:** What questions do you still have?

Then choose **one important observation, idea, or question** to share with the class (in class: Domino Discover).
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## 🔑 Check your thinking (try it first!)

- **See:** The thermometer at the equator warmed the most and the one near the pole warmed the least. Light hitting at a **low angle** is **spread over more squares**, so each square gets less energy. As the tilted globe moved around the lamp, the light hit NYC **more directly in June** and at a **lower angle in December**, and the opposite for Melbourne.
- **Think:** The **angle** of sunlight, not the distance, controls how much a place heats up. Because the axis stays tilted the same way, each hemisphere takes turns leaning toward the Sun.
- **Wonder:** *Do places also get more hours of sunlight in summer? Do all places on Earth get the same amount of light on the same day? Why is Earth closest to the Sun in January?*
:::

## Part 2: Using Computational and Visual Models {#ss-part2}

### Part D: Sunlight Around the World {#ss-part-d}

In class you used the [Seasons and Ecliptic Simulator](https://astro.unl.edu/naap/motion1/animations/seasons_ecliptic.html) (University of Nebraska-Lincoln). The map below is a computational model of the same thing: it calculates where it is **day** and **night** at **noon in London (12:00 UTC)** on any date.

**Conferring questions:** How is sunlight affecting different parts of the world? Are all areas of the globe receiving the same amount of light? How do you think the difference in light affects each area?

```{ojs}
  const rows = [
    {place: "North Pole (90° N)", lat: 90}, {place: "Arctic Circle (66.6° N)", lat: 66.56}, {place: "NYC (40.7° N)", lat: 40.7},
    {place: "Equator (0°)", lat: 0}, {place: "Melbourne (37.8° S)", lat: -37.8}, {place: "Antarctic Circle (66.6° S)", lat: -66.56}, {place: "South Pole (90° S)", lat: -90}
  ];
  const fmtH = h => h <= 0.01 ? "0 h (dark all day)" : h >= 23.99 ? "24 h (Sun never sets)" : `${h.toFixed(1)} h`;
  const tbl = document.createElement("div");
  tbl.style.overflowX = "auto";
  tbl.innerHTML = `<table class="ss-table"><thead><tr><th>Place</th><th>Daylight</th><th>Noon Sun angle</th><th>Sunlight energy (daily avg., W/m²)</th></tr></thead><tbody>` +
    rows.map(r => `<tr><td>${r.place}</td><td>${fmtH(ssDayLen(r.lat, dec))}</td><td>${ssNoon(r.lat, dec).toFixed(0)}°</td><td>${ssInsol(r.lat, ssMapDay).toFixed(0)}</td></tr>`).join("") +
    `</tbody></table>`;
  const box = html`<div></div>`;
  box.appendChild(plot);
  if (!ssLand) box.appendChild(html`<p class="ss-note">🗺️ The coastlines could not load, but day and night are still shown.</p>`);
  box.appendChild(tbl);
  box.appendChild(html`<p class="ss-note">Calculated from Earth's tilt and orbit. Sunlight energy is the daily average at the top of the atmosphere (before clouds). Daylight ignores the bending of light by air, which adds a few minutes.</p>`);
  return box;
}
```

### ✏️ In your Student Explain Guide: Questions 1 and 2

With a partner (or on your own):

1. **June/July:** Why is it **summer in NYC** and **winter in Melbourne**? Use evidence from the models (Sun angle, spread of light, daylight hours).
2. **December/January:** Why are the seasons **reversed**? What is the same about Earth's tilt, and what is different about Earth's position?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## 🔑 Check your thinking: Questions 1 and 2 (try it first!)

1. **June/July:** Earth's **Northern Hemisphere is tilted toward the Sun**. Sunlight hits NYC at a **high angle (about 73° at noon)**, so it is concentrated on a small area, and NYC gets **about 15 hours** of daylight. More energy → warmer → **summer (about 24–25 °C)**. Melbourne is in the hemisphere tilted **away**: low Sun (**about 29°**), spread-out light, **about 9.5 hours** of daylight → **winter (about 10–11 °C)**.
2. **December/January:** The tilt **still points the same direction in space**, but Earth is now on the **other side of its orbit**, so the **Southern Hemisphere** leans toward the Sun. Melbourne gets high-angle light (**about 76°**) and **about 14.5 hours** of daylight (summer). NYC gets low-angle light (**about 26°**) and **about 9 hours** (winter). Earth is actually **closest** to the Sun in early January, so distance isn't the cause.
:::

**Formal terms for what you explored:**

| Term | Meaning | Where you saw it |
|---|---|---|
| **Insolation** | Incoming solar radiation: sunlight energy reaching a surface | Parts A–D |
| **Angle of insolation** | How high the Sun is above the horizon. Higher angle = more concentrated energy | Part B grid paper |
| **Axial tilt** | Earth's axis is tilted about **23.5°** and always points toward **Polaris** | Part C |
| **Revolution** | Earth's yearly trip around the Sun (365¼ days) | Part C |
| **Rotation** | Earth's daily spin (about 24 hours). Causes day and night, **not** seasons | Part C |
| **Summer solstice** | About **June 21** (N. Hemisphere): Sun overhead at the **Tropic of Cancer (23.5° N)**; longest day in the north | Parts C, D |
| **Winter solstice** | About **December 21** (N. Hemisphere): Sun overhead at the **Tropic of Capricorn (23.5° S)**; shortest day in the north | Parts C, D |
| **Equinox** | About **March 20** and **September 22**: Sun overhead at the **equator**; about 12 h of day and night everywhere | Part D |
| **Perihelion / aphelion** | Earth's closest (about **147.1 million km**, early January) and farthest (about **152.1 million km**, early July) points | Part C |

## A General Explanation for Seasons {#ss-q3}

::: {.student-task}
### ✏️ In your Student Explain Guide: Question 3 (poster)

In class, groups made a poster that explains **how seasons happen anywhere on Earth** and shared it in an **Idea Carousel**. Make your own version. Include:

- A **model** (drawing) of Earth at **two or more positions** in its orbit, with the **tilted axis** pointing the same way
- How the **angle of sunlight** and **hours of daylight** change for each hemisphere
- A **claim** with **evidence** (data from Parts A–D, the temperature graph) and **reasoning** (why more direct sunlight means warmer temperatures)
:::

**Questions to test your model** (from the Class Consensus Discussion):

- What **evidence** do you have for your explanation?
- What is the **mechanism**? What are the science ideas involved?
- How **confident** do you feel about your claims? Why?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## 🔑 Check your general explanation (try it first!)

**Claim:** Seasons happen because **Earth's axis is tilted (about 23.5°)** and keeps pointing the same direction in space as Earth **revolves around the Sun**. This changes **how directly** and **for how long** sunlight hits each hemisphere.

**Evidence:**

- Part A: the spot where light hit most directly warmed the most (about 12 °C) and the spot where light hit at a low angle warmed the least (about 3 °C).
- Part B: light at 30° is spread over **twice** the area of light at 90°, so each square gets **half** the energy.
- Parts C and D: in June the noon Sun is about **73°** in NYC and **29°** in Melbourne, with about **15 h** vs **9.5 h** of daylight; in December it's reversed.
- Temperatures: NYC is warmest in July (about 26 °C) and Melbourne is warmest in January–February (about 21 °C).
- Earth is **closest** to the Sun in **January**, during NYC's winter, so distance is not the cause.

**Reasoning:** Sunlight heats Earth. When a hemisphere is **tilted toward the Sun**, sunlight arrives at a **higher angle** (more concentrated) and for **more hours each day**, so it absorbs more energy and warms up: **summer**. Six months later, that hemisphere is **tilted away**, sunlight is **spread out** and days are **shorter**: **winter**. Because the hemispheres lean in opposite directions, their seasons are **opposite**.
:::

## Class Consensus Ideas: Seasons {#ss-consensus}

::: {.key-idea}
**🔑 Class Consensus Ideas: Seasons**

- **Sunlight provides heat** for Earth.
- Places receiving **more direct sunlight** become **hotter** than places receiving less direct sunlight.
- Because of the **tilt**, the **Northern Hemisphere is tilted away from the Sun** for half the year. It is **colder** and the **days are shorter**: **Northern Hemisphere winter**.
- At that same time, the **Southern Hemisphere is tilted toward the Sun**, with **longer days** and **warmer** temperatures: **Southern Hemisphere summer**.
- For the other half of the year, the **Northern Hemisphere is tilted toward the Sun**: longer days, warmer, **Northern Hemisphere summer**.
- During that time, the **Southern Hemisphere is tilted away**: colder, shorter days, **Southern Hemisphere winter**.
:::

In class, ideas the group wasn't sure about were marked with a **question mark (?)**. Write down any ideas you still have a question mark on. They're a good guide for what to review.

# Looking Ahead: From Seasons to Long-Term Climate {#ss-bridge}

::: {.elaborate-box}
## 🔭 Bridge to Earth-Sun Dynamics

Seasons are a **yearly** cycle. Climate change happens over **decades to hundreds of thousands of years**, and very different mechanisms control global temperature over those long times. But the key idea from this chapter still matters: **how much sunlight reaches each part of Earth** controls temperature.

Earth's orbit and tilt aren't fixed. Over very long times they slowly change:

| Orbital factor | What changes | About how long one cycle takes |
|---|---|---|
| **Tilt** | Earth's tilt wobbles between about **22.1° and 24.5°** | about **41,000 years** |
| **Shape of the orbit** (eccentricity) | The orbit stretches from nearly circular to slightly oval | about **100,000 years** |
| **Direction of tilt** (precession) | The axis slowly swings like a spinning top, changing **which month** each hemisphere leans toward the Sun | about **26,000 years** |
:::

Try changing the tilt. How would seasons in NYC change?

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof ssBridgeTilt = Inputs.range([22.1, 24.5], {step: 0.1, value: 23.4, label: "Earth's tilt (°):"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const e = ssBridgeTilt;
  const jun = ssInsol(65, 172, e, false), decQ = ssInsol(65, 355, e, false);
  const nycS = 90 - (40.7 - e), nycW = 90 - (40.7 + e);
  return html`<div class="ss-cards">
    <div class="ss-card"><span class="lab">NYC noon Sun, June</span><b class="big">${nycS.toFixed(1)}°</b></div>
    <div class="ss-card"><span class="lab">NYC noon Sun, December</span><b class="big">${nycW.toFixed(1)}°</b></div>
    <div class="ss-card"><span class="lab">Summer sunlight at 65° N</span><b class="big">${jun.toFixed(0)} W/m²</b>June solstice daily average</div>
    <div class="ss-card"><span class="lab">Winter sunlight at 65° N</span><b class="big">${decQ.toFixed(0)} W/m²</b>December solstice daily average</div>
  </div><p class="ss-note">Same computational model as Part D (Earth–Sun distance held constant). 65° N is where the big ice sheets of past ice ages grew.</p>`;
}
```

**Up next:** In [Earth-Sun Dynamics](unit4-earth-sun-dynamics.qmd), you'll compare these slow orbital changes with **ice core temperature records** and **solar cycles** to figure out whether natural factors can explain the warming and melting ice we see **today**.

# Chapter Summary

| Key Concept | Details |
|---|---|
| **Seasons** | A yearly, repeating cycle of temperature and daylight; opposite in the two hemispheres |
| **Cause** | Earth's **23.5° tilt** + **revolution** around the Sun, with the axis always pointing toward Polaris |
| **Angle of insolation** | Higher Sun angle → light concentrated on a smaller area → more heating. At 30°, light covers 2× the area of 90° |
| **Daylight hours** | The hemisphere tilted toward the Sun has longer days (NYC: about 15 h in June, about 9 h in December) |
| **Summer** | Your hemisphere is tilted **toward** the Sun: high Sun, long days, more energy |
| **Winter** | Your hemisphere is tilted **away**: low Sun, short days, less energy |
| **Solstices** | About Jun 21 (Sun overhead at 23.5° N) and Dec 21 (Sun overhead at 23.5° S) |
| **Equinoxes** | About Mar 20 and Sep 22: Sun overhead at the equator, about 12 h of daylight everywhere |
| **Not distance** | Closest to the Sun (about 147.1 million km) in early **January**, during NYC's winter; only about a 3% change |
| **Latitude** | Equator: warm all year, small seasons (Singapore about 27–29 °C). Middle and high latitudes: big seasons |
| **Looking ahead** | Tilt, orbit shape, and direction of tilt change over tens of thousands of years, changing climate over long timescales |

# Myth or Fact?

```{=html}
<div id="ss-myths" style="background:linear-gradient(135deg,#0b1020 0%,#12324a 55%,#0f4c4a 100%); color:white; padding:30px; border-radius:16px; margin:30px 0; font-family:'Inter',sans-serif; box-shadow:0 20px 60px rgba(0,0,0,0.3);">
  <h2 style="font-family:'Space Grotesk',sans-serif; font-size:1.8em; margin:0 0 8px 0; color:#fde68a !important;">
    ☀️ Seasons: Myths vs. Facts
  </h2>
  <p style="color:#cbd5e1; margin:0 0 20px 0; font-size:0.95em;">Decide whether each statement is a MYTH or a FACT!</p>
  <div style="display:flex; justify-content:space-between; align-items:center; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:6px; background:rgba(255,255,255,0.05); padding:12px 20px; border-radius:12px; margin-bottom:20px;">
    <div id="ssmf-progress" style="color:#cbd5e1; font-size:0.9em;">Card 1 of 8</div>
    <div style="color:#cbd5e1; font-size:0.9em;">Score: <span id="ssmf-score" style="color:#fbbf24; font-weight:700;">0</span> / <span id="ssmf-total">0</span></div>
  </div>
  <div id="ssmf-card" style="background:rgba(255,255,255,0.08); border-radius:14px; padding:28px; min-height:100px; display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; text-align:center; font-size:1.1em; font-weight:600; line-height:1.6; border:1.5px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.1);"></div>
  <div style="display:flex; gap:12px; margin-top:16px;">
    <button id="ssmf-myth" onclick="ssmfAnswer('Myth')" style="flex:1; min-height:44px; padding:14px; border:none; border-radius:10px; background:linear-gradient(135deg,#e17055,#d63031); color:white; font-size:1em; font-weight:700; cursor:pointer;">❌ MYTH</button>
    <button id="ssmf-fact" onclick="ssmfAnswer('Fact')" style="flex:1; min-height:44px; padding:14px; border:none; border-radius:10px; background:linear-gradient(135deg,#00b894,#00866e); color:white; font-size:1em; font-weight:700; cursor:pointer;">✅ FACT</button>
  </div>

  <button id="ssmf-next" onclick="ssmfNext()" style="display:none; margin-top:12px; width:100%; min-height:44px; padding:12px; border:2px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.2); border-radius:10px; background:transparent; color:white; font-size:0.95em; font-weight:600; cursor:pointer;">Next Card →</button>
  <div id="ssmf-done" style="display:none; text-align:center; padding:20px;">
    <div style="font-size:2.5em; margin-bottom:10px;">🎉</div>

    <button onclick="ssmfRestart()" style="margin-top:12px; min-height:44px; padding:10px 24px; border:2px solid #fbbf24; border-radius:20px; background:transparent; color:#fbbf24; font-size:0.9em; cursor:pointer; font-weight:600;">Play Again</button>
  </div>
</div>
<script>
(function() {
  var cards = [
    { text: "It's summer when Earth is closer to the Sun and winter when it's farther away.", type: "Myth",
      explanation: "Earth is closest to the Sun (about 147.1 million km) in early January, which is winter in NYC, and farthest (about 152.1 million km) in early July. The distance changes only about 3%. Seasons come from the tilt, which changes the angle of sunlight and the length of the day." },
    { text: "Earth is closest to the Sun in early January.", type: "Fact",
      explanation: "Perihelion (closest point) is around January 3. That's summer in the Southern Hemisphere but winter in the Northern Hemisphere, which shows distance isn't what makes summer." },
    { text: "When it's summer in New York City, it's winter in Melbourne, Australia.", type: "Fact",
      explanation: "In June and July the Northern Hemisphere is tilted toward the Sun and the Southern Hemisphere is tilted away. NYC averages about 24–26 °C, while Melbourne averages about 10–11 °C." },
    { text: "The hemisphere tilted toward the Sun is warmer because the tilt brings it much closer to the Sun.", type: "Myth",
      explanation: "Tilting moves a hemisphere only a few thousand kilometers closer, out of about 150 million km, so that's not why. It's warmer because sunlight hits it at a higher angle (more concentrated) and for more hours each day." },
    { text: "Low-angle sunlight spreads the same energy over a larger area, so each spot heats up less.", type: "Fact",
      explanation: "That's what the grid paper showed. Light at 30° covers twice the area of light at 90°, so each square gets half the energy. It's also why the Sun feels weaker in winter and early morning." },
    { text: "Earth's axis flips to point the other way halfway through the year.", type: "Myth",
      explanation: "The axis keeps pointing the same direction in space (toward Polaris) all year. What changes is where Earth is in its orbit, so first one hemisphere and then the other leans toward the Sun." },
    { text: "Seasons happen because Earth spins faster in summer.", type: "Myth",
      explanation: "Earth rotates once about every 24 hours all year long. Rotation causes day and night. The seasons come from revolution around the Sun with a tilted axis." },
    { text: "On the June solstice, the North Pole gets more total sunlight in a day than the equator does.", type: "Fact",
      explanation: "With 24 hours of daylight, the North Pole gets about 520 W/m² averaged over the day (at the top of the atmosphere) vs. about 385 W/m² at the equator. It stays cold because the Sun is always low, ice reflects much of the light, and it's dark for months in winter." }
  ];
  var idx = 0, score = 0, answered = 0, cardAnswered = false;
  function el(id) { return document.getElementById(id); }
  function updateCard() {
    if (idx >= cards.length) {
      el('ssmf-card').style.display = 'none';
      el('ssmf-myth').style.display = 'none';
      el('ssmf-fact').style.display = 'none';
      el('ssmf-feedback').style.display = 'none';
      el('ssmf-next').style.display = 'none';
      el('ssmf-done').style.display = 'block';
      el('ssmf-final').textContent = score;
      el('ssmf-count').textContent = cards.length;
      return;
    }
    el('ssmf-card').textContent = cards[idx].text;
    el('ssmf-progress').textContent = 'Card ' + (idx + 1) + ' of ' + cards.length;
    el('ssmf-feedback').style.display = 'none';
    el('ssmf-next').style.display = 'none';
    el('ssmf-myth').disabled = false;
    el('ssmf-fact').disabled = false;
    el('ssmf-myth').style.opacity = '1';
    el('ssmf-fact').style.opacity = '1';
    cardAnswered = false;
  }
  window.ssmfAnswer = function(choice) {
    if (cardAnswered) return;
    cardAnswered = true;
    answered++;
    var card = cards[idx];
    var correct = (choice === card.type);
    if (correct) score++;
    el('ssmf-score').textContent = score;
    el('ssmf-total').textContent = answered;
    var fb = el('ssmf-feedback');
    fb.style.display = 'block';
    fb.style.background = correct ? 'rgba(0,184,148,0.2)' : 'rgba(214,48,49,0.2)';
    fb.style.border = '1px solid ' + (correct ? '#00b894' : '#e17055');
    fb.innerHTML = '<strong>' + (correct ? '✅ Correct! ' : '❌ That\'s a ' + card.type + '! ') + '</strong>' + card.explanation;
    el('ssmf-myth').disabled = true;
    el('ssmf-fact').disabled = true;
    el('ssmf-myth').style.opacity = (choice === 'Myth') ? '1' : '0.5';
    el('ssmf-fact').style.opacity = (choice === 'Fact') ? '1' : '0.5';
    el('ssmf-next').style.display = 'block';
  };
  window.ssmfNext = function() { idx++; updateCard(); };
  window.ssmfRestart = function() {
    idx = 0; score = 0; answered = 0;
    el('ssmf-card').style.display = 'flex';
    el('ssmf-myth').style.display = 'block';
    el('ssmf-fact').style.display = 'block';
    el('ssmf-done').style.display = 'none';
    el('ssmf-score').textContent = '0';
    el('ssmf-total').textContent = '0';
    updateCard();
  };
  updateCard();
})();
</script>
```

# End-of-Chapter Quiz {#end-of-chapter-quiz}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
function buildSsQuiz(id, title, questions) {
  const outer = html`<div id="${id}" style="font-family:'Inter',sans-serif; max-width:720px; margin:18px auto;"></div>`;
  const header = html`<div style="background:linear-gradient(135deg,#0f766e 0%,#1e40af 100%);color:#fff;border-radius:14px 14px 0 0;padding:18px 24px;">
    <div style="font-size:1.1em;font-weight:700;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;"><span style="font-size:1.2em;">📝</span> ${title}</div>
    <div style="font-size:0.85em;opacity:0.9;margin-top:4px;">Select an answer for each question.</div>
  </div>`;
  const body = html`<div style="border:1.5px solid #99d5cf;border-top:none;border-radius:0 0 14px 14px;overflow:hidden;background:#f0fdfa;padding:16px;"></div>`;
  questions.forEach((qq, qi) => {
    const card = document.createElement("div");
    card.style.cssText = "background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;border-radius:12px;padding:16px 20px;margin-bottom:14px;box-shadow:0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.08);";
    card.innerHTML = `<p style="font-weight:700;margin:0 0 10px;color:#1e1b4b;">${qi+1}. ${qq.q}</p>`;
    qq.options.forEach((opt, oi) => {
      const btn = document.createElement("button");
      btn.textContent = opt;
      btn.style.cssText = "display:block;width:100%;min-height:44px;text-align:left;padding:10px 14px;margin:6px 0;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;cursor:pointer;font-size:.95em;transition:border-color .2s,background .2s;";
      btn.onmouseover = () => { if(!card.dataset.answered){ btn.style.borderColor="#0f766e";btn.style.background="#f0fdfa"; }};
      btn.onmouseout  = () => { if(!card.dataset.answered){ btn.style.borderColor="#e2e8f0";btn.style.background="#fff"; }};
      btn.onclick = () => {
        if(card.dataset.answered) return;
        card.dataset.answered = "true";
        card.querySelectorAll("button").forEach(b => {
          b.style.cursor="default"; b.onmouseover=null; b.onmouseout=null;
          b.style.borderColor="#e2e8f0"; b.style.background="#f8fafc"; b.style.color="#475569";
        });
        if(oi === qq.correct){
          btn.style.borderColor="#48bb78";btn.style.background="#f0fff4";btn.style.color="#276749";btn.style.fontWeight="700";
          fb.innerHTML = "✅ Correct! " + qq.explanation;
          fb.style.color="#276749";fb.style.background="#f0fff4";
        } else {
          btn.style.borderColor="#fc8181";btn.style.background="#fff5f5";btn.style.color="#9b2c2c";btn.style.fontWeight="700";
          const correctBtn = card.querySelectorAll("button")[qq.correct];
          correctBtn.style.borderColor="#48bb78";correctBtn.style.background="#f0fff4";correctBtn.style.color="#276749";correctBtn.style.fontWeight="700";
          fb.innerHTML = "❌ " + qq.explanation;
          fb.style.color="#9b2c2c";fb.style.background="#fff5f5";
        }
        fb.style.padding="10px 14px";fb.style.marginTop="8px";fb.style.borderRadius="8px";
      };
      card.appendChild(btn);
    });
    const fb = document.createElement("div");
    fb.style.cssText = "border-radius:8px;font-size:.9em;transition:all .3s;";
    card.appendChild(fb);
    body.appendChild(card);
  });
  outer.appendChild(header);
  outer.appendChild(body);
  return outer;
}
```
